name: Improve your handwriting
blurb: Adult handwriting improves surprisingly fast because the problems are mechanical: grip, arm movement, letter shape and consistency, all of which are directly fixable.
gear: A pen you enjoy writing with
steps: Diagnose your current hand: write a paragraph, then mark the specific failures — inconsistent slant, uneven height, poor spacing, malformed letters.
Fix the grip: relaxed tripod, pen resting on the middle finger, no white knuckles.
Move from the arm and shoulder rather than the fingers. Finger-writing is what makes handwriting cramped and tiring.
Drill the basic shapes: rows of ovals and parallel lines, which is where consistency actually comes from.
Rebuild the letters you form worst, one at a time, with a chosen model.
Write a page a day, deliberately slowly, and only speed up once the shapes hold.
tips: Slow down. Almost all bad handwriting is a speed problem, not a shape problem.
Consistency reads as neatness. Even a slightly odd letterform looks good when it is identical every time.
proof: A page of your natural-speed handwriting is comfortably legible and consistent, side by side with your before sample.
